intuition.title: Ethylenediamine and the low-temperature route
intuition.text: The authors propose that ethylenediamine coordinates copper, disperses the reagent and mediates heat and growth. They observe CuI dissolving slowly and the liquid changing from transparent through light to dark blue. This interpretation is not an isolated-complex structure or measured kinetic mechanism.

intuition.title: Source-proposed iodide reduction
intuition.text: The displayed reaction uses CuI and selenium to produce Cu2−xSe and iodine. The authors attribute selenium reduction to iodide and argue that precipitation drives the reaction; iodine is said to be removed in washing. This is their mechanistic account, not a separately measured iodine yield.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Displayed reaction and final mechanism paragraph

intuition.title: Temperature and time boundaries
intuition.text: The main optimum is90 °C for4 h. Lower temperature or shorter time gives incomplete reaction, lower yield/crystallinity and residual Se/CuI by XRD; exact tested points are not supplied. Below50 °C the reaction does not start. Higher temperature or longer time enlarges grains; only180 °C for4 h is numerically linked to a100 nm XRD estimate.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Reaction-condition discussion across columns

intuition.title: Keep measurement scope and printed anomalies visible
intuition.text: TEM average/range, XRD coherent grain estimate and XPS surface ratio describe different measurements of the main product. The180 °C comparison has only a reported XRD size. The printed57.4 nm cell constant and284.60 kV C1s reference remain unresolved source anomalies and are not silently repaired.

general_background.title: Solvent and a closed reaction environment
general_background.summary: A heated closed solvent environment changes solubility, transport and precursor conversion compared with an open vessel. Changes in solvent properties and dissolution followed by reprecipitation can alter the pathways available for nucleation and crystal growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
